steps.u: Speed up our GitHub Actions pipeline, it takes 14 minutes. Most of it is npm install and the Docker build.

steps.r:
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    with: { node-version: 20 }
  - run: npm ci
  - run: npm test
  - run: docker build -t shop:${{ github.sha }} .

i.new_string:
- uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
  - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
    with:
      context: .
      tags: shop:${{ github.sha }}
      cache-from: type=gha
      cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

steps.r:
FROM node:20
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm ci
RUN npm run build

i.content:
FROM node:20 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

steps.a: I cached the npm download, switched the image build to buildx with the GitHub Actions layer cache, and reordered the Dockerfile so the dependency layer is only rebuilt when package files change. I can't run the workflow from here, so the timing improvement is expected but unmeasured.

reference.summary: Reworked the CI pipeline for speed: npm caching in setup-node, a buildx Docker build with the GitHub Actions layer cache, and a Dockerfile reordered so dependencies install in their own cached layer. The workflow could not be run here, so the speed-up is unmeasured.
